title: Peacock Inn with Jimmy Jones's band, WOW radio and singing "All of Me"
summary: Jones recalls 30 weeks at the Peacock Inn, pay with tips, letters from Kansas City friends, and singing hit tunes on WOW radio.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: .....You had to get married, you see... They didn't take no singles, you know. I couldn't understand that. I said, "What has that got to do with music?" As we know today you take a chance with a man who's got responsibilities. You know what's so funny? When my daughter was born -
Was that the first born one, your daughter?
The second born; I lost my first.
And the second one was your daughter. What's her name?

Joanne. When my first was born, Milt, I was making $5 a week with comebacks. You know what a comeback is? All right, now I'm going to tell you something. I have it in my scrapbook. We were working at the Peacock Inn at 19th and Farnum; stayed there 30 weeks with Jimmy Jones's band. Now we were making we started out at thought around $35 a week. We begin to get letters from Ben Webster, from Paul Webster, from Basie, from everybody.
* a tip, money in the kitty

We thought that they were in Kansas City making $100 a week. This is Depression! You see, and these people were asking for jobs; they heard our broadcast. We were on WOW. I was the first one to sing "All of Me" on the radio. Scotty was the vocalist so he would pick the tunes.

Guitar. He would pick the tunes. "You can have this one." "Penthouse Serenade," all of those things; I took those things. I was the first one to sing them over the radio because I found out something years ago. From 1930 I had met a chanteuse by the name of Clara Campbell and she used to always write in to New York into Tin Pan Alley and get these songs that's going to be the hit.

The lead sheets. You had the lead sheets and had a violin score, you see, and I would get these things and learn these things. I wasn't smoking and drinking then, you see, and you got the megaphone to the mike which later on when I was going to go to the (Nebraska) Lincoln University to be with Lee Bennett at KFAB that went to Jan Garber he was going to be the second Bing Crosby and Russ Colombo, you know what I mean.
